Rebecca =E2=80=94

I've spent most of the weekend going through the documents and thinking about=
 where we need to land on this ground lease, so apologies for the Sunday nigh=
t email, but I want to get this to you and Jordan before our call tomorrow so=
 you can hit the ground running.

As you know, we executed the term sheet with Paul Castignetti on behalf of th=
e City of Port Calloway Redevelopment Authority on June 10. I've been reviewi=
ng that term sheet alongside the title commitment (TC-2025-07821 from Ridgepo=
int Title & Escrow Co., effective June 1, 2025), the Phase II ESA from Halcyo=
n Environmental Consultants Inc. (dated May 2, 2025), and the construction lo=
an term sheet from Bayside Federal Lending Corp. (dated May 28, 2025). I've c=
ross-referenced all of them and I have a pretty clear picture of what I need =
from you in the lease draft.

The purpose of this email is to lay out my priorities and specific concerns s=
o you and Jordan can prepare a first draft of the ground lease agreement and =
get it to Howard Koss at Pryor Whitfield & Koss LLP as quickly as possible. O=
ur target Lease Commencement Date is October 1, 2025, which gives us roughly =

 counsel, the Authority's outside counsel, Coventry's team, and a municipal b=
oard that doesn't meet every week.

One more piece of context to frame everything below: total project cost is $4=
25 million =E2=80=94 $285 million in construction financing from Bayside Fede=
ral, $95 million in equity from Coventry Capital Partners LP, and $45 million=
 co-invested by Meridian. There is a lot of capital at stake, and the ground =
lease is the document that everything else rests on. If the lease is deficien=
t, the entire capital stack comes apart.

**1. Overall Priorities**

I have four overarching priorities, and everything else flows from these:

*First, protect the leasehold investment.* This is a 99-year ground lease on =
a 3.2-acre parcel =E2=80=94 APN 127-003-0045, 10-30 Pier Street, Port Callowa=
y, CT 06801 =E2=80=94 with $425 million in total development cost. The improv=
ements we're building on this land will be worth multiples of the land value =
over the life of the lease. The ground lease must be airtight on Tenant prote=
ctions. We are the party taking the real economic risk here, and the lease ne=
eds to reflect that.

*Second, ensure financeability.* Sandra Milliken at Bayside Federal has been =
crystal clear: the construction loan will not close unless the ground lease i=
s "bankable." Separately, Ansel Coventry (cc'd here) has confirmed that Coven=
try Capital Partners LP requires the ground lease to be "institutional qualit=
y" =E2=80=94 meaning it must satisfy not just Bayside's specific requirements=
, but the requirements of any institutional lender that might participate in =
a refinancing over the life of a 99-year term. We are going to refinance this=
 project multiple times. The ground lease has to work for a lender in 2025 an=
d a lender in 2065.

*Third, maximize the tax abatement benefit.* The Authority offered a 15-year =
phased tax abatement, and we need every dollar of it to make the pro forma wo=
rk, especially in the early years when we're still in construction and lease-=
up. More on this below.

*Fourth, push back hard on the reverter/forfeiture provisions.* The reverter =
clause as described in the term sheet is a dealbreaker in its current form. T=
his is my single biggest concern and I've devoted a full section to it below.

**2. Reverter Right and Improvement Forfeiture =E2=80=94 This Is the Hill**

Rebecca, I need you to spend significant time on this because it is the issue=
 that could kill the deal.

Here's what the term sheet says: If Meridian fails to meet Milestone 1 (comme=
ncement of construction by April 1, 2027) or Milestone 3 (substantial complet=
ion of Phase 1 =E2=80=94 the residential tower and ground-floor retail =E2=80=
=94 by October 1, 2030), the Authority can terminate the ground lease on 180 =
days' written notice. Upon termination under the reverter, Tenant forfeits th=
e $5,700,000 security deposit AND =E2=80=94 this is the part that keeps me up=
 at night =E2=80=94 "all improvements constructed to date revert to the Autho=
rity without compensation."

I understand the Authority's position. They've been sitting on this waterfron=
t parcel for years, they've had developers fail to perform before, and they w=
ant enforcement teeth. I get it. But what's described in the term sheet is no=
t a reasonable enforcement mechanism =E2=80=94 it's unconscionable. By the ti=
me Milestone 3 is at issue, Meridian could have $200 to $300 million of const=
ruction in the ground. Steel, concrete, mechanical systems, curtain wall =E2=
=80=94 real, physical improvements with real value. The idea that all of that=
 reverts to the Authority without any compensation whatsoever is not commerci=
ally reasonable, and frankly, I doubt it would hold up in court.

I'd like you to research whether Connecticut law provides any relief against =
this kind of disproportionate forfeiture. I recall from a prior deal =E2=80=
=94 I think it was the Stamford project =E2=80=94 that there's a legal princi=
ple disfavoring penalties that are grossly disproportionate to the actual har=
m suffered. I could be misremembering the specifics, so I'll leave it to you =
to confirm the legal basis and whether it applies here.

What I want in the lease is one of two things: either (a) a fair market value=
 buyout of any improvements upon a reverter termination =E2=80=94 meaning the=
 Authority gets the land back but pays Tenant the appraised FMV of the improv=
ements as of the termination date =E2=80=94 or, at minimum, (b) reimbursement=
 of Tenant's actual, unreimbursed hard construction costs, net of any insuran=
ce proceeds received and less the Authority's actual, documented damages resu=
lting from Tenant's delay or failure to perform. I'm open to discussing the f=
ormula, but the baseline principle is non-negotiable: the Authority does not =
get hundreds of millions of dollars of improvements for free. That is not a r=
emedy, it's a windfall.

Now, here's where this connects directly to the financing, and this is critic=
al.

Sandra Milliken at Bayside Federal has told me point-blank that the reverter =
right as written would jeopardize the leasehold mortgage. Think about it from=
 Bayside's perspective: they're making a $285 million construction loan secur=
ed by a leasehold mortgage. If the Authority can terminate the lease and wipe=
 out $285 million in construction loan collateral simply because we miss a mi=
lestone =E2=80=94 even if Meridian is 95% complete and the delay was caused b=
y a permitting holdup or a supply chain issue =E2=80=94 no lender will touch =
this deal. Sandra was unequivocal about that.

I need you to ensure the following protections are built into the ground leas=
e:

- The reverter right must be expressly subordinate to any leasehold mortgage.=
 The Authority cannot exercise the reverter in a manner that extinguishes the=
 leasehold mortgagee's security interest without the protections described be=
low.

- Bayside (or any future leasehold mortgagee) must receive simultaneous writt=
en notice of any alleged milestone default, and the lender must have an indep=
endent cure period =E2=80=94 I'd suggest at least 180 days from the date of t=
he lender's receipt of notice =E2=80=94 during which the lender can cure the =
milestone default, including by exercising the right to install a replacement=
 developer or property manager.

- The "New Lease" right from Bayside's construction loan term sheet must surv=
ive a reverter termination. Meaning: if the ground lease is terminated for an=
y reason (including reverter), the leasehold mortgagee must have the right to=
 obtain a new ground lease on substantially the same terms and conditions, fo=
r the remainder of the original term.

- The Authority cannot exercise the reverter without the leasehold mortgagee =
having first exhausted its full cure period. Ideally, I'd want the Authority =
to need the lender's written consent before exercising a reverter, but I reco=
gnize that may be a bridge too far in negotiations. At minimum, the lender's =
cure period must be a hard prerequisite.

I cannot overstate this: if we can't reconcile the reverter with Bayside's re=
quirements, this deal does not close. Period.

**3. Percentage Rent**

I want to talk about the percentage rent provision. As negotiated, Meridian p=
ays 2.0% of Gross Revenues in excess of a $28,500,000 annual breakpoint, comm=
encing in Year 6 of the lease.

The Authority pushed hard on percentage rent as a way to participate in the p=
roject's upside, and we agreed in principle =E2=80=94 I think it's fair for t=
he municipality to share in the success of a project built on public land. I'=
m not trying to eliminate percentage rent. But I am uncomfortable with how th=
is is currently structured, and I want you to look at it carefully.

The breakpoint was set based on current revenue projections =E2=80=94 our 202=
5 pro forma assumptions about rental rates, occupancy, and commercial lease t=
erms. But this is a 99-year lease. The economic assumptions we're making toda=
y are going to be wildly off in 20 years, let alone 50 or 75. I'm worried tha=
t the way this is written, the percentage rent could become an outsized burde=
n over time as the project matures and revenues grow, even in periods when th=
e project is performing at exactly the level both sides anticipated when we s=
truck this deal. We agreed to a participation mechanism, not a permanent gros=
s revenue tax. I need you to structure this so it works fairly over the life =
of the lease =E2=80=94 so that both sides get what they intended at the negot=
iating table, not just in Year 6, but in Year 60. Make sure the economics sta=
y in line with what both sides intended.

Also, please make sure "Gross Revenues" is defined tightly. I want to exclude=
 security deposits, utility reimbursements, insurance proceeds, condemnation =
awards, and any pass-throughs to tenants that are not true revenue to Meridia=
n. If a subtenant is reimbursing us for their share of common area maintenanc=
e, that is not revenue. I don't want to be paying percentage rent on cost rec=
overy.

**4. Tax Abatement**

The 15-year phased tax abatement is a cornerstone of the project economics. T=
he structure in the term sheet is:

- Years 1=E2=80=935: 25% of full assessed value
- Years 6=E2=80=9310: 50% of full assessed value
- Years 11=E2=80=9315: 75% of full assessed value
- Thereafter: full assessment

The Authority's appraiser projects a post-development assessed value of $178,=
000,000, and the current mill rate is 34.75 mills. At full assessment, we'd b=
e paying over $6.1 million a year in property taxes. The phase-in is what mak=
es the early-year economics viable =E2=80=94 it gives us breathing room durin=
g lease-up and stabilization when we're carrying the construction debt and ne=
ed every dollar of NOI to service the loan and meet coverage ratios.

I want to make sure we get the full benefit of all 15 years of the abatement =
when it matters =E2=80=94 during the operating period when we're actually gen=
erating revenue and need the tax relief. With a 36-month construction period =
before rent commencement, the timing of when the abatement kicks in is import=
ant. Please structure this so that we're maximizing the abatement benefit dur=
ing the income-producing years. That's what the Authority intended when they =
offered this incentive, and it's what makes the deal pencil.

I've discussed this extensively with Ansel, and Coventry's underwriting assum=
es the full 15-year abatement applies during the income-producing years. Thei=
r equity return model is built on those assumptions. If the numbers don't wor=
k, Coventry won't fund. It's that straightforward.

*Security deposit:* The $5,700,000 letter of credit represents 24 months of b=

*Affordable housing:* The term sheet includes a 15% affordable housing covena=
nt. Meridian is committed to this and our project architect is already incorp=

*Development milestones:* For reference, the milestones are: Milestone 1 =E2=

ctural completion by April 1, 2029; Milestone 3 =E2=80=94 Phase 1 substantial=
 completion (residential tower and retail) by October 1, 2030; Milestone 4 =
=E2=80=94 Phase 2 substantial completion by October 1, 2032. The force majeur=
e extensions are 12 months in the aggregate plus an additional 6 months speci=
fically for permitting delays. I think these are tight but workable. Let's ma=
ke sure the force majeure definition is comprehensive =E2=80=94 the standard =
laundry list of acts of God, labor disputes, governmental delays, etc.

*Assignment:* I understand the Authority has a right of first refusal during =
the first 20 years for any assignment of the ground lease to a non-affiliated=
 entity. I assume you'll handle the mechanics of this so it doesn't interfere=
 with the financing or any future recapitalization.

**6. Timeline and Process**

I need to stress urgency here. Our target Lease Commencement Date is October =
1, 2025. The Authority Board has already adopted Resolution No. 2025-047 on J=
une 5, 2025, authorizing Paul Castignetti to negotiate and execute the ground=
 lease on behalf of the Authority. On our side, Bayside Federal's constructio=

**[TERM SHEET --- LONG-TERM GROUND LEASE]{.underline}**

**10-30 Pier Street, Port Calloway, Connecticut 06801**

**June 10, 2025**

**EXECUTED --- BINDING TERM SHEET**

This Term Sheet sets forth the principal business terms and conditions upon which the City of Port Calloway Redevelopment Authority (as Landlord) and Meridian Gateway Holdings LLC (as Tenant) intend to negotiate and execute a definitive long-term ground lease agreement (the \"Definitive Lease\" or \"Ground Lease Agreement\") for the property located at 10-30 Pier Street, Port Calloway, Connecticut 06801, as more particularly described herein. This Term Sheet is binding upon the parties with respect to the exclusivity obligations set forth in Section 19 and the mutual obligation to negotiate the Definitive Lease in good faith. Upon execution and delivery of the Definitive Lease, the Definitive Lease shall supersede this Term Sheet in its entirety, and this Term Sheet shall be of no further force or effect. This Term Sheet has been negotiated between the parties with the assistance of Hargrove & Linden LLP (Tenant\'s Counsel) and Pryor Whitfield & Koss LLP (Landlord\'s Counsel).

**[Section 1: Parties]{.underline}**

**Landlord/Lessor:**

City of Port Calloway Redevelopment Authority (the \"Authority\" or \"Landlord\"), a public body corporate and politic organized and existing under the provisions of Connecticut General Statutes § 8-125 et seq., with its principal offices located at 75 Municipal Plaza, Port Calloway, Connecticut 06801. The Authority is governed by a Board of Commissioners and is authorized to enter into this Term Sheet and the contemplated Definitive Lease pursuant to its enabling legislation and applicable resolutions of its Board of Commissioners. The Executive Director of the Authority is Paul Castignetti. The Chair of the Board of Commissioners is Diana Forsythe.

**Tenant/Lessee:**

Meridian Gateway Holdings LLC (the \"Tenant\"), a Delaware limited liability company duly formed on August 14, 2019, and registered to do business in the State of Connecticut, with its principal place of business at 400 Harborview Drive, Suite 1200, Port Calloway, Connecticut 06801. The Managing Member of Tenant is Marcus Ellison. Tenant\'s Employer Identification Number is 84-2917635. Tenant is a special purpose entity formed for the purpose of developing and operating the Project (as defined herein) on the Premises (as defined herein).

**Tenant\'s Counsel:**

Hargrove & Linden LLP, 1100 Constitution Avenue, Hartford, Connecticut 06103. Lead Partner: Rebecca Tsang. Associate Counsel: Jordan Abernathy.

**Landlord\'s Counsel:**

Pryor Whitfield & Koss LLP, 55 Courthouse Square, Port Calloway, Connecticut 06801. Lead Attorney: Howard Koss.

**[Section 2: The Premises / Parcel Description]{.underline}**

The property that is the subject of this Term Sheet and the contemplated Definitive Lease (the \"Premises\") is described as follows:

**Property Address:** 10-30 Pier Street, Port Calloway, Connecticut 06801.

**Assessor\'s Parcel Number:** 127-003-0045.

**Approximate Size:** 3.2 acres (139,392 square feet), as determined by the most recent records of the Port Calloway Tax Assessor\'s office, subject to confirmation by the ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey to be prepared and attached to the Definitive Lease.

**Location:** The Premises are situated within the Port Calloway Waterfront Revitalization District (the \"WRD\") and are zoned WRD-3 (Mixed-Use High Density) under the Port Calloway Zoning Regulations.

**Boundaries:** The Premises are generally bounded as follows:

> • **North:** Pier Street (a public right-of-way);
>
> • **East:** Long Island Sound waterfront promenade (subject to a public pedestrian access easement);
>
> • **South:** Assessor\'s Parcel No. 127-003-0044, which is retained by the Authority for future park development and is not part of the Premises;
>
> • **West:** Harbor Avenue (a public right-of-way).

**Waterfront Features:** The Premises include approximately 480 linear feet of bulkhead frontage along the Long Island Sound waterfront on the eastern boundary.

**Flood Zone Designation:** The Premises are located within FEMA Flood Zone AE, with a Base Flood Elevation (\"BFE\") of 12 feet NAVD88, as depicted on the applicable Flood Insurance Rate Map. All habitable space within the Project shall be constructed at a finished floor elevation of no less than 15 feet NAVD88, providing a minimum of three (3) feet of freeboard above the BFE, in compliance with the Port Calloway Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance and applicable building code requirements.

**Legal Description:** The precise metes-and-bounds legal description of the Premises shall be derived from the ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey to be commissioned by Tenant and attached as an exhibit to the Definitive Lease.

**Title Commitment:** Ridgepoint Title & Escrow Co. has issued Title Commitment No. TC-2025-07821, with an effective date of June 1, 2025 (Title Officer: James Harwood), confirming the Landlord\'s fee simple interest in the Premises. The title commitment is subject to certain exceptions as further described in Section 13 hereof.

**Landlord\'s Title:** The Authority holds fee simple title to the Premises, having acquired the same through eminent domain proceedings conducted pursuant to Connecticut General Statutes § 8-128, which proceedings were concluded by final judgment entered in 2012 in the Connecticut Superior Court, Judicial District of Port Calloway.

**[Section 3: Lease Term]{.underline}**

**Lease Commencement Date:** October 1, 2025 (targeted), subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions precedent set forth in Section 15 of this Term Sheet.

**Lease Term:** Ninety-nine (99) years, measured from the Lease Commencement Date.

**Lease Expiration Date:** September 30, 2124, unless the Lease is sooner terminated in accordance with its terms.

**Rent Commencement Date:** The \"Rent Commencement Date\" shall be the earlier to occur of: (a) thirty-six (36) months following the Lease Commencement Date (i.e., October 1, 2028, based on the targeted Lease Commencement Date), or (b) the date upon which the first temporary or permanent certificate of occupancy is issued by the Port Calloway Building Official for any portion of the Project. During the period between the Lease Commencement Date and the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant shall have no obligation to pay Base Rent or Percentage Rent, but shall be responsible for all real property taxes, assessments, insurance premiums, and other carrying costs associated with the Premises as provided herein.

No renewal options are contemplated. The ninety-nine (99) year term constitutes the full and complete duration of the ground lease.

**[Section 4: Project Description and Permitted Uses]{.underline}**

**Project Overview:** Tenant intends to develop on the Premises a mixed-use development project (the \"Project\") comprising the following principal components:

> \(a\) A twenty-eight (28) story residential rental tower (the \"Residential Tower\") containing a number of residential dwelling units to be determined and specified in the Definitive Lease, including ground-floor residential lobby and amenity spaces (fitness center, package room, resident lounge, and leasing office), with residential dwelling units located on floors 2 through 28;
>
> \(b\) A six (6) story Class A office building (the \"Office Building\");
>
> \(c\) Ground-floor retail space distributed throughout the Project, designed to activate the streetscape along Pier Street, Harbor Avenue, and the waterfront promenade; and
>
> \(d\) Accessory structured and/or below-grade parking facilities sufficient to serve the residential, office, and retail components of the Project in accordance with applicable zoning requirements.

**Permitted Uses:** The Premises may be used for the following purposes, and for no other purpose: residential apartments (for rent only; no condominiums or cooperative units), Class A office, ground-floor retail (excluding adult entertainment establishments, firearms sales, pawnshops, and gasoline service stations), restaurants (including those with liquor service licensed by the Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection), and accessory parking. No industrial, manufacturing, or warehousing uses shall be permitted on the Premises.

**Affordable Housing Requirement:** A minimum of fifteen percent (15%) of residential units within the Project shall be designated as affordable housing, available to households earning at or below eighty percent (80%) of Area Median Income (\"AMI\") as published annually by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for the Port Calloway Metropolitan Statistical Area, for the duration of the Lease Term. This affordable housing covenant shall be incorporated into the Definitive Lease and shall run with the leasehold interest.

**Public Open Space:** The Project shall include a minimum of eight thousand (8,000) square feet of publicly accessible open space on the waterfront (eastern) side of the Premises, designed and maintained by Tenant at its sole cost and expense, and connected to the existing public pedestrian promenade running along the Long Island Sound waterfront. The design and programming of the public open space shall be subject to Landlord\'s reasonable approval in connection with the site plan review process.

**Environmental Restrictions:** All uses of the Premises and all development activity conducted thereon must comply with the Environmental Land Use Restriction (\"ELUR\") recorded on March 22, 2018, at Volume 412, Page 88 of the Port Calloway Land Records. The ELUR restricts residential use on the ground floor of any structure erected on the Premises and requires the installation and maintenance of an engineered barrier (cap) for any ground disturbance activity on the Premises. Tenant acknowledges the existence of the ELUR and agrees that all Project design, construction, and operation shall conform to its requirements. Additional detail regarding environmental obligations is set forth in Section 7 of this Term Sheet.

**[Section 5: Base Rent]{.underline}**

**Initial Annual Base Rent:** Two Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,850,000) per year (approximately \$20.45 per square foot per year based on 139,392 square feet of Premises area) (\$20.45 per SF × 139,392 SF = approximately \$2,850,000 per year), payable in equal monthly installments of Two Hundred Thirty-Seven Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$237,500) (\$2,850,000 ÷ 12 = \$237,500), commencing on the Rent Commencement Date. All payments of Base Rent shall be due on the first day of each calendar month, without demand, setoff, or deduction except as expressly provided in the Definitive Lease.

**Rent Escalation --- Fixed Component (Lease Years 1 through 15):** Beginning on the first day of Lease Year 1 (which shall be the Rent Commencement Date) and continuing through the end of Lease Year 15, Base Rent shall be subject to a fixed annual escalation of two and one-half percent (2.5%) per annum, compounding annually, with adjustments implemented at five (5) year intervals as follows:

> • **Lease Years 1 through 5:** \$2,850,000 per year (\$237,500 per month).
>
> • **Lease Years 6 through 10:** \$3,224,500 per year (\$2,850,000 × (1.025)\^5 ≈ \$3,224,500) (approximately \$268,708 per month).
>
> • **Lease Years 11 through 15:** \$3,648,200 per year (\$3,224,500 × (1.025)\^5 ≈ \$3,648,200) (approximately \$304,017 per month).

**Rent Escalation --- CPI Component (Lease Year 16 and Thereafter):** Beginning in Lease Year 16 and at each subsequent ten (10) year interval thereafter, Base Rent shall be reset to the greater of:

> \(a\) The amount that would result from the continued application of the two and one-half percent (2.5%) per annum compounding fixed escalation from the initial Base Rent of \$2,850,000, calculated as of the applicable reset date; or
>
> \(b\) The initial Base Rent of \$2,850,000, adjusted by the cumulative percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, Northeast Region (CPI-U Northeast) (Series ID: CUUR0100SA0), as published by the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics, from the Lease Commencement Date through the applicable reset date. In the event the CPI-U Northeast ceases to be published, a comparable successor index shall be used.

CPI-based resets shall occur at the following Lease Year intervals: Lease Years 16, 26, 36, 46, 56, 66, 76, 86, and 96.

The Definitive Lease shall set forth in detail the methodology for calculating the CPI adjustment, including the reference month for the base index and each reset index, the rounding convention, and any dispute resolution mechanism applicable to the determination of the CPI-adjusted rent.

**[Section 6: Percentage Rent]{.underline}**

**Percentage Rent Obligation:** Beginning in Lease Year 6 and continuing for the remainder of the Lease Term, Tenant shall pay to Landlord additional rent in the form of Percentage Rent equal to two percent (2.0%) of the annual Gross Revenues of the Project in excess of Twenty-Eight Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$28,500,000) (the \"Breakpoint\").

**Definition of Gross Revenues:** For purposes of this Section 6, \"Gross Revenues\" shall mean all rents, fees, charges, and other income of every kind generated from the operation of the Project, including but not limited to residential rental income, office rental income, retail rental income, parking revenues, and all other ancillary income derived from the Premises or the improvements thereon. Specific exclusions from Gross Revenues (such as security deposits not applied to rent, proceeds of insurance claims, condemnation awards, and similar items) shall be defined in the Definitive Lease.

**Payment:** Percentage Rent, if any, shall be calculated and payable on an annual basis, due within ninety (90) days following the end of each Lease Year. Each payment of Percentage Rent shall be accompanied by a certified statement of Gross Revenues for the applicable Lease Year, prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles consistently applied, signed by an authorized representative of Tenant. Tenant shall maintain complete and accurate books and records relating to Gross Revenues for a period of not less than three (3) years following the end of each Lease Year.

**Breakpoint:** The \$28,500,000 annual Breakpoint is a fixed dollar amount and shall remain unchanged for the duration of the Lease Term.

**Landlord Audit Right:** Landlord shall have the right, exercisable no more than once per Lease Year, to audit or cause to be audited by an independent certified public accountant Tenant\'s books, records, and financial statements relating to Gross Revenues, upon not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to Tenant. If an audit reveals an underpayment of Percentage Rent of five percent (5%) or more for any audited Lease Year, Tenant shall reimburse Landlord for the reasonable costs of the audit. All audits shall be conducted during regular business hours at Tenant\'s principal place of business.

**[Section 7: Remediation Credit and Environmental Obligations]{.underline}**

**Environmental Conditions:** The parties acknowledge the results of the following environmental assessments of the Premises, both prepared by Halcyon Environmental Consultants Inc. (Principal Environmental Scientist: Dr. Lena Okafor):

> • **Phase I Environmental Site Assessment**, dated March 15, 2025, which identified recognized environmental conditions associated with the historical use of the Premises as a marine industrial facility; and
>
> • **Phase II Environmental Site Assessment**, dated May 2, 2025, which confirmed the presence of petroleum hydrocarbon contamination in two areas of the Premises, as follows:
>
> \(1\) **Northwest Corner Area:** Approximately 4,200 square feet of impacted soil, with total petroleum hydrocarbons (\"TPH\") detected at concentrations up to 3,800 mg/kg, which exceeds the applicable Connecticut Remediation Standard Regulations (\"RSR\") Residential Direct Exposure Criteria (\"RDEC\") threshold of 500 mg/kg; and
>
> \(2\) **Former Dry Dock Area:** Approximately 1,600 square feet of impacted soil, with TPH detected at concentrations up to 1,200 mg/kg, which also exceeds the RSR RDEC threshold of 500 mg/kg.

**Environmental Land Use Restriction (ELUR):** An Environmental Land Use Restriction was recorded against the Premises on March 22, 2018, at Volume 412, Page 88 of the Port Calloway Land Records, in connection with a prior remediation action. The ELUR restricts residential use on the ground floor of any structure erected on the Premises and requires the installation and maintenance of an engineered barrier (cap) over any areas of ground disturbance to prevent direct contact with residual soil contamination. All development and use of the Premises must comply with the terms and conditions of the ELUR.

**Total Estimated Remediation Cost:** The total estimated cost of remediation to achieve compliance with the Connecticut Remediation Standard Regulations and the ELUR is Two Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,400,000), allocated as follows: \$1,850,000 for the Northwest Corner Area and \$550,000 for the Former Dry Dock Area.

**Landlord Remediation Credit:** Landlord shall provide to Tenant a credit in the aggregate amount of One Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$1,800,000) (the \"Remediation Credit\") against Base Rent, to be applied against the first monthly rent payments due after the Rent Commencement Date as follows:

> • Months 1 through 7: Monthly Base Rent payments of \$237,500 each shall be reduced to \$0 (\$237,500 × 7 = \$1,662,500 in credits applied through month 7);
>
> • Month 8: Partial credit of \$137,500 applied (\$1,800,000 − \$1,662,500 = \$137,500), with Tenant paying the remaining balance of \$100,000 (\$237,500 − \$137,500 = \$100,000) in month 8; and
>
> • Month 9 and thereafter: Full monthly Base Rent of \$237,500 resumes.

**Tenant\'s Remediation Responsibility:** Tenant shall be responsible for the remaining Six Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$600,000) of the estimated remediation cost (\$2,400,000 total less \$1,800,000 Remediation Credit), to be borne by Tenant at its sole cost and expense. Tenant shall also be responsible for any actual remediation costs in excess of the \$2,400,000 estimate.

**Remediation Standard:** All remediation work shall be performed in compliance with the Connecticut Remediation Standard Regulations (Regs. Conn. State Agencies § 22a-133k-1 et seq.) and the terms and conditions of the ELUR. Tenant shall engage a Licensed Environmental Professional (\"LEP\") to oversee and certify the completion of all remediation activities.

**Ongoing Environmental Compliance:** Following completion of remediation, Tenant shall be responsible for all ongoing environmental compliance obligations, including maintenance and monitoring of the engineered barrier/cap, periodic reporting to the Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (\"DEEP\"), and compliance with all applicable environmental laws and regulations for the duration of the Lease Term.

**[Section 8: Security Deposit]{.underline}**

**Amount:** Five Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$5,700,000), equal to twenty-four (24) months of the initial monthly Base Rent (\$237,500 × 24 = \$5,700,000).

**Form:** The security deposit shall be provided in the form of an irrevocable standby letter of credit issued by a commercial bank organized under the laws of the United States or any state thereof, having a minimum credit rating of A- from Standard & Poor\'s or A3 from Moody\'s Investors Service (or an equivalent rating from a nationally recognized credit rating agency). The letter of credit shall be in a form reasonably acceptable to Landlord and shall name the Authority as beneficiary.

**Reduction:** The letter of credit amount shall be reduced to Two Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,850,000), equal to twelve (12) months of the initial Base Rent, upon Tenant\'s demonstration to Landlord\'s reasonable satisfaction that the Project has achieved and maintained an overall occupancy rate of ninety percent (90%) or greater for a period of twenty-four (24) consecutive months.

**Application:** Landlord may draw upon the letter of credit upon the occurrence of any uncured Event of Default by Tenant, subject to the notice and cure provisions to be set forth in the Definitive Lease. Any amounts drawn by Landlord shall be applied to Tenant\'s outstanding obligations under the Lease. Tenant shall, within thirty (30) days following any draw by Landlord, replenish the letter of credit to the required amount.

**Replacement and Renewal:** Tenant shall maintain the letter of credit in full force and effect throughout the Lease Term. If the letter of credit has an expiration date, Tenant shall deliver to Landlord a replacement or renewal letter of credit not later than thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the then-current letter of credit. Failure to timely deliver a replacement or renewal letter of credit shall constitute an Event of Default under the Definitive Lease.

**[Section 9: Development Milestones and Reverter Rights]{.underline}**

**Development Milestones:** Tenant shall achieve the following development milestones within the specified time periods, as measured from the Lease Commencement Date:

> **Milestone 1 --- Commencement of Construction:** Within eighteen (18) months of the Lease Commencement Date (by April 1, 2027). \"Commencement of Construction\" shall mean the physical pouring of footings for at least one building within the Project, following the issuance of all necessary building permits by the Port Calloway Building Department.
>
> **Milestone 2 --- Completion of Structural Frame (Residential Tower):** Within forty-two (42) months of the Lease Commencement Date (by April 1, 2029). \"Completion of Structural Frame\" shall mean the topping-out of the structural steel and/or concrete frame for the Residential Tower.
>
> **Milestone 3 --- Substantial Completion of Phase 1 (Residential Tower and Retail):** Within sixty (60) months of the Lease Commencement Date (by October 1, 2030). \"Substantial Completion\" shall mean the issuance of a temporary or permanent certificate of occupancy for the Residential Tower and ground-floor retail space, such that the Residential Tower is ready for residential occupancy and the retail space is available for tenant fit-out.
>
> **Milestone 4 --- Substantial Completion of Phase 2 (Office Building):** Within eighty-four (84) months of the Lease Commencement Date (by October 1, 2032). \"Substantial Completion\" shall mean the issuance of a temporary or permanent certificate of occupancy for the Office Building.

**Force Majeure Extension:** The deadlines for achievement of the foregoing milestones shall be extended on a day-for-day basis for delays caused by Force Majeure Events, up to a maximum aggregate extension of twelve (12) months across all milestones. \"Force Majeure Events\" shall mean acts of God, war, terrorism, civil unrest, strikes, labor disputes, governmental orders or moratoria, pandemics, epidemics, and similar events beyond Tenant\'s reasonable control. In addition, the milestone deadlines shall be extended for up to six (6) additional months in the aggregate for delays attributable to governmental permitting processes beyond Tenant\'s reasonable control, including delays in the issuance of building permits, zoning approvals, or environmental permits. The total aggregate extension for Force Majeure Events and permitting delays shall not exceed eighteen (18) months.

**Reverter Rights:** If Tenant fails to achieve Milestone 1 or Milestone 3 (as extended for Force Majeure Events and permitting delays as provided above), Landlord may exercise a reverter right by delivering written notice to Tenant specifying the milestone failure. Upon receipt of such notice, Tenant shall have one hundred eighty (180) calendar days to cure the milestone failure (the \"Milestone Cure Period\"). If Tenant fails to achieve the applicable milestone within the Milestone Cure Period, the Lease shall automatically terminate upon the expiration of such period, and:

> \(a\) Tenant shall forfeit the security deposit (the \$5,700,000 letter of credit), which Landlord shall be entitled to draw in full; and
>
> \(b\) All improvements, structures, and fixtures constructed, installed, or placed on the Premises by Tenant as of the date of termination shall immediately revert to and become the sole property of the Landlord, free and clear of any claims by Tenant, without any payment, compensation, or reimbursement to Tenant.

**Lender Protections (Construction Financing):** The parties acknowledge that the Project will be financed in part by a construction loan and that the construction lender will require certain protections in connection with the ground lease structure. Accordingly, the Definitive Lease shall include the following provisions:

> *Leasehold Mortgage.* Tenant shall have the right to encumber its leasehold interest in the Premises with a leasehold mortgage (or deed of trust) in favor of a recognized institutional lender, subject to the terms and conditions of the Definitive Lease.
>
> *SNDA.* Landlord shall enter into a Subordination, Non-Disturbance, and Attornment Agreement (\"SNDA\") with Tenant\'s construction lender on customary terms and conditions, substantially in the form to be attached to the Definitive Lease as an exhibit.
>
> *New Lease Right.* In the event the Lease is terminated due to an Event of Default by Tenant, the leasehold mortgagee (or its designee) shall have the right to obtain a new lease of the Premises on substantially the same terms and conditions as the terminated Lease (a \"New Lease\"), provided that the leasehold mortgagee: (i) cures all monetary defaults within sixty (60) days following the date of termination; and (ii) cures all non-monetary defaults within ninety (90) days following the date of termination, or, if such non-monetary default is of a nature that cannot reasonably be cured within ninety (90) days, commences cure within such ninety (90) day period and thereafter diligently prosecutes such cure to completion.
>
> *Default Notices.* Landlord shall deliver copies of all notices of default, notices of termination, and any other material notices under the Lease to the leasehold mortgagee simultaneously with delivery to Tenant, at such address as the leasehold mortgagee may designate in writing.
>
> *No Voluntary Surrender.* Landlord shall not accept a voluntary surrender, cancellation, or modification of the Lease from Tenant without the prior written consent of the leasehold mortgagee.
>
> *Foreclosure and Assignment.* The leasehold mortgagee shall have the right to foreclose on the leasehold interest (whether by judicial or non-judicial proceedings, deed-in-lieu of foreclosure, or otherwise) and to assign the Lease to a qualified transferee without Landlord\'s consent, provided that any such transferee meets reasonable financial and experience qualifications to be established in the Definitive Lease.

**[Section 10: Taxes, Assessments, and Tax Abatement]{.underline}**

**Triple-Net Structure:** The Definitive Lease shall be structured as a triple-net ground lease. Tenant shall be solely responsible for the payment of all real property taxes, special assessments, governmental charges, and other impositions of every kind levied or assessed against the Premises and/or the improvements thereon throughout the Lease Term. Tenant\'s tax obligations shall include all ad valorem real property taxes, special assessments, benefit assessments, sewer and water charges, and any future taxes, fees, or governmental charges hereafter imposed on the Premises or the improvements by any federal, state, or municipal taxing authority.

**Current Assessment:** The Premises are currently assessed by the Port Calloway Tax Assessor at Four Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$4,200,000) (land only, no improvements). The current effective mill rate for the City of Port Calloway is 34.75 mills, yielding estimated current annual real property taxes of approximately One Hundred Forty-Five Thousand Nine Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$145,950) (\$4,200,000 × 0.03475 = \$145,950).

**Post-Development Projected Assessment:** Following completion of the Project, the combined assessed value of the Premises (land and improvements) is projected to be approximately One Hundred Seventy-Eight Million Dollars (\$178,000,000), based on the Authority\'s current assessment methodology and market projections. At the current mill rate of 34.75 mills, the estimated annual real property taxes following full build-out would be approximately Six Million One Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$6,185,500) (\$178,000,000 × 0.03475 = \$6,185,500). The parties acknowledge that actual assessed values and mill rates may vary over the Lease Term and that the foregoing projections are estimates only.

**Tax Abatement Program:** The Authority has offered, and the parties have agreed to, a fifteen (15) year tax abatement program for the Project, structured as a phase-in of the post-development tax assessment as follows:

> • **Years 1 through 5:** Tenant shall pay real property taxes calculated on twenty-five percent (25%) of the full post-development assessed value. Estimated annual taxes during this phase: \$1,546,375 (\$178,000,000 × 0.25 × 0.03475).
>
> • **Years 6 through 10:** Tenant shall pay real property taxes calculated on fifty percent (50%) of the full post-development assessed value. Estimated annual taxes during this phase: \$3,092,750 (\$178,000,000 × 0.50 × 0.03475).
>
> • **Years 11 through 15:** Tenant shall pay real property taxes calculated on seventy-five percent (75%) of the full post-development assessed value. Estimated annual taxes during this phase: \$4,639,125 (\$178,000,000 × 0.75 × 0.03475).
>
> • **Year 16 and thereafter:** The full post-development assessed value shall apply, and Tenant shall pay real property taxes on one hundred percent (100%) of the assessed value, without abatement.

**Abatement Commencement:** The fifteen (15) year tax abatement period shall commence on the Lease Commencement Date. The Authority shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain all approvals and authorizations necessary to implement the tax abatement program, including any required action by the Port Calloway Board of Finance or the Connecticut Office of Policy and Management.

**[Section 11: Assignment, Subletting, and Right of First Refusal]{.underline}**

**Assignment Restrictions:** Tenant shall not assign the Lease or any interest therein to any person or entity that is not an Affiliate (as defined below) of Tenant without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and subject to the Landlord\'s Right of First Refusal as described below. Any purported assignment in violation of this provision shall be void and of no force or effect.

**Subletting:** Tenant may sublease individual units or portions of the Project to residential tenants, office tenants, and retail tenants in the ordinary course of the Project\'s operation without the need for Landlord\'s prior written consent. Any sublease of the entire Premises, or of substantially all of the Premises, to a single subtenant shall require Landlord\'s prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

**Right of First Refusal (ROFR):** During the first twenty (20) years of the Lease Term (i.e., from the Lease Commencement Date through September 30, 2045), if Tenant proposes to assign the Lease or any interest therein to a non-Affiliate entity, Landlord shall have a right of first refusal to repurchase the leasehold interest on the same terms and conditions as the proposed assignment. Tenant shall provide written notice to Landlord (the \"Assignment Notice\") setting forth the identity of the proposed assignee, the material terms and conditions of the proposed assignment (including the proposed purchase price), and a copy of the proposed assignment agreement or letter of intent. Landlord shall have sixty (60) calendar days following receipt of the Assignment Notice to exercise the ROFR by delivering written notice of exercise to Tenant. If Landlord does not exercise the ROFR within the sixty (60) day period, Tenant may proceed with the proposed assignment to the identified assignee on terms no more favorable to the assignee than those set forth in the Assignment Notice.

**Affiliated Transfers:** Transfers, assignments, and conveyances to Affiliates of Tenant shall be permitted without Landlord\'s consent and without triggering the ROFR. For purposes of this Section, \"Affiliate\" shall mean: (a) any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Tenant; (b) any entity in which Marcus Ellison holds a direct or indirect controlling interest; (c) Coventry Capital Partners LP and its affiliates, subsidiaries, and related funds; and (d) any entity resulting from an internal reorganization or restructuring of Tenant\'s ownership, provided that Marcus Ellison or Coventry Capital Partners LP (or their respective affiliates) retain a controlling interest in the resulting entity.

**Lender Foreclosure/Assignment:** The leasehold mortgagee\'s right to foreclose on the leasehold interest and assign the Lease to a qualified transferee is set forth in Section 9 of this Term Sheet.

> \(d\) The filing of a voluntary petition in bankruptcy by Tenant, the entry of an order for relief against Tenant in any involuntary bankruptcy proceeding that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days, or the making by Tenant of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors; and
>
> \(e\) Any material misrepresentation by Tenant in this Term Sheet, the Definitive Lease, or any document delivered in connection therewith.

**Landlord Remedies:** Upon the occurrence of an uncured Event of Default by Tenant, Landlord shall have the right to: terminate the Lease upon applicable notice; draw on the letter of credit security deposit; exercise the reverter rights described in Section 9; and pursue any and all other remedies available at law or in equity.

**Landlord Events of Default:** Failure by Landlord to perform or observe any material obligation under the Lease within thirty (30) days following written notice from Tenant specifying such failure, or, if such failure is of a nature that cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, failure by Landlord to commence cure within such thirty (30) day period and thereafter diligently prosecute such cure to completion.

**Tenant Remedies:** Upon the occurrence of an uncured Event of Default by Landlord, Tenant shall have the right to: offset amounts due against Base Rent; seek specific performance of Landlord\'s obligations; and pursue any and all other remedies available at law or in equity, including an action for damages.

The foregoing is a summary only. The complete default and remedies provisions shall be set forth in the Definitive Lease.

**[Section 17: Casualty and Condemnation (Summary)]{.underline}**

The Definitive Lease shall include customary provisions addressing casualty damage and condemnation of the Premises, which the parties anticipate will include the following principal elements:

> \(a\) In the event of casualty damage to the improvements, Tenant shall be obligated to restore the improvements to their pre-casualty condition using available insurance proceeds, subject to the terms and conditions of the Lease and any leasehold mortgage;
>
> \(b\) During the period of restoration following a casualty, Tenant shall be entitled to an abate of Base Rent proportionate to the portion of the Premises rendered unusable;
>
> \(c\) If the casualty renders the Premises or a material portion thereof unsuitable for the Permitted Uses and restoration is not economically feasible (as determined by criteria to be set forth in the Definitive Lease), either party shall have the right to terminate the Lease;
>
> \(d\) In the event of a total or partial condemnation of the Premises, the condemnation award shall be allocated between Landlord and Tenant as follows: Landlord shall receive the portion of the award attributable to the value of the fee interest in the land, and Tenant shall receive the portion attributable to the value of the leasehold interest and the improvements; and
>
> \(e\) In the event of a partial condemnation that does not render the Premises unsuitable for the Permitted Uses, Tenant shall restore the remaining improvements to the extent practicable, and Base Rent shall be equitably adjusted to reflect the reduction in usable area.

The complete casualty and condemnation provisions shall be negotiated and set forth in the Definitive Lease.

**[Section 18: End of Term / Surrender]{.underline}**

Upon the expiration of the Lease Term on September 30, 2124, or upon any earlier termination of the Lease in accordance with its terms, all improvements, buildings, structures, and fixtures located on the Premises shall become the sole property of the Landlord without any payment, compensation, or reimbursement to Tenant. Tenant shall surrender the Premises to Landlord in good condition, reasonable wear and tear excepted, free and clear of all liens, encumbrances, and tenancies (other than those approved by Landlord).

During the final ten (10) years of the Lease Term (i.e., from and after October 1, 2114), Tenant shall not undertake any alterations, renovations, or capital improvements to the Premises or the improvements thereon in excess of a threshold dollar amount to be established in the Definitive Lease without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

The Definitive Lease will include provisions addressing Tenant\'s right to remove its trade fixtures, personal property, and movable equipment at the expiration or earlier termination of the Lease Term, provided that Tenant repairs any damage to the Premises caused by such removal.

**[Section 19: Miscellaneous Provisions]{.underline}**

**Governing Law:** This Term Sheet and the Definitive Lease shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Connecticut, without regard to conflicts of law principles.

**Dispute Resolution:** The Definitive Lease will include dispute resolution provisions, which the parties anticipate will provide for mandatory mediation as a condition precedent to litigation. If mediation is unsuccessful, disputes shall be resolved by litigation in the Connecticut Superior Court, Judicial District of Port Calloway.

**Notices:** All notices, consents, demands, and other communications required or permitted under this Term Sheet or the Definitive Lease shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given when delivered by hand, sent by nationally recognized overnight courier service, or mailed by certified or registered mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, to the addresses set forth in Section 1 of this Term Sheet, or to such other address as either party may designate by written notice to the other.

**Confidentiality:** The parties acknowledge that the Authority is a public body subject to the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-200 et seq.), and that certain terms of this Term Sheet and the Definitive Lease may be subject to public disclosure pursuant to applicable law. Subject to the requirements of the Freedom of Information Act, the parties agree to treat the terms and conditions of this Term Sheet and the negotiations relating to the Definitive Lease as confidential to the extent permitted by law.

**Binding Nature:** This Term Sheet is binding upon the parties solely with respect to: (a) the obligation of each party to negotiate the Definitive Ground Lease Agreement in good faith; and (b) the exclusivity provisions set forth below. All other provisions of this Term Sheet are non-binding expressions of the parties\' mutual intent and shall not create any enforceable rights or obligations until the execution and delivery of the Definitive Lease, except as otherwise expressly provided herein.

**Exclusivity Period:** From the date of execution of this Term Sheet through December 31, 2025 (the \"Exclusivity Period\"), the Authority shall not negotiate, solicit offers from, or enter into any agreement with any other party regarding the lease, sale, or other disposition of the Premises. Tenant shall use commercially reasonable efforts to negotiate and execute the Definitive Lease during the Exclusivity Period.

**Authority Approvals:** The Definitive Lease shall be subject to final review and approval by the Authority\'s Board of Commissioners, acting by duly adopted resolution at a properly noticed public meeting in accordance with the Authority\'s bylaws and applicable law.

**Broker:** No broker, finder, or other intermediary has been engaged by either party in connection with this transaction. Each party represents and warrants to the other that it has not dealt with any broker or finder, and each party shall indemnify and hold harmless the other from and against any claims for brokerage commissions or finder\'s fees arising from a breach of this representation.

(\"Lender\") is pleased to present this Construction Loan Term Sheet (this \"Term Sheet\") to Meridian Gateway Holdings LLC (\"Borrower\") setting forth the indicative terms and conditions under which Lender would consider providing the construction financing described herein for the above-referenced project. **[Section 1: Parties and Project Summary]{.underline}**

**Borrower:** Meridian Gateway Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (EIN: 84-2917635), with principal offices at 400 Harborview Drive, Suite 1200, Port Calloway, CT 06801. Managing Member: Marcus Ellison.

**Guarantor(s):**

> \(a\) Marcus Ellison (individual) --- limited recourse/carve-out guaranty, as more fully described in Section 4 hereof.
>
> \(b\) Coventry Capital Partners LP, a Delaware limited partnership, with offices at 780 Post Road, Greenwich, CT 06830 (Managing Partner: Ansel Coventry III) --- completion guaranty, as more fully described in Section 4 hereof.

**Lender:** Bayside Federal Lending Corp., a Connecticut-chartered commercial bank, with principal offices at 200 Atlantic Boulevard, Stamford, CT 06902.

**Project Description:** Construction of a mixed-use waterfront development (the \"Project\") on an approximately 3.2-acre (139,392 SF) parcel located at 10-30 Pier Street, Port Calloway, CT 06801, within the Port Calloway Waterfront Revitalization District (WRD), zoned WRD-3 (Mixed-Use High Density). The Project comprises: (a) a 28-story residential tower containing rental apartments, of which no fewer than fifteen percent (15%) shall be designated as affordable housing units available to households earning at or below eighty percent (80%) of Area Median Income (\"AMI\") as determined by HUD; (b) a 6-story Class A office building; and (c) ground-floor retail space. The Project also includes a minimum of 8,000 square feet of publicly accessible open space on the waterfront side of the parcel and approximately 480 linear feet of bulkhead along the waterfront.

Executive Director: Paul Castignetti. Commissioner/Chair: Diana Forsythe.

**Borrower\'s Counsel:** Hargrove & Linden LLP, 1100 Constitution Avenue, Hartford, CT 06103 (Lead Partner: Rebecca Tsang; Associate: Jordan Abernathy).

**Ground Lessor\'s Counsel:** Pryor Whitfield & Koss LLP, 55 Courthouse Square, Port Calloway, CT 06801 (Lead Attorney: Howard Koss).

**[Section 2: Loan Terms]{.underline}**

**Loan Amount:** \$285,000,000 (Two Hundred Eighty-Five Million Dollars).

**Loan Type:** Construction loan, interest-only during the construction period.

**Interest Rate:** The Secured Overnight Financing Rate (\"SOFR\"), as published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York (or any successor administrator), plus two hundred seventy-five basis points (2.75%) per annum, calculated on the basis of actual days elapsed in a 360-day year. SOFR shall be subject to a floor of 0.50% (fifty basis points); in no event shall the applicable SOFR rate used for interest calculations be less than 0.50% per annum.

**Term:** Forty-eight (48) months from the date of closing (the \"Initial Maturity Date\"), with two (2) six (6)-month extension options (each, an \"Extension Period\"), for a total potential term of sixty (60) months from closing (the \"Extended Maturity Date\"). Each extension shall be subject to the satisfaction of the following conditions at the time of the extension request: (i) no Event of Default or event that, with the giving of notice or the passage of time, would constitute an Event of Default shall exist; (ii) payment of the applicable extension fee; (iii) delivery of an updated appraisal satisfactory to Lender; and (iv) achievement of specified construction progress milestones as set forth in the approved construction schedule.

**Origination Fee:** 1.00% of the Loan Amount (\$2,850,000), earned in full upon closing and payable at closing from loan proceeds or Borrower\'s equity.

**Extension Fee:** 0.25% of the then-outstanding principal balance, payable on the first day of each Extension Period.

**Repayment:** Interest-only during the construction period. The entire outstanding principal balance, together with all accrued and unpaid interest, fees, and other amounts owing under the loan documents, shall be due and payable in full on the Initial Maturity Date (or the Extended Maturity Date, if applicable).

**Prepayment:** Prepayment of all or any portion of the outstanding principal balance shall be permitted without penalty or premium at any time after the first twelve (12) months following closing. During the first twelve (12) months following closing, prepayment shall be subject to a prepayment premium equal to 1.00% of the amount prepaid.

**Default Rate:** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, interest shall accrue at a rate equal to the contractual rate (SOFR + 275 bps) plus an additional four hundred basis points (4.00%) per annum (i.e., SOFR + 675 bps).

**Late Charge:** A late charge of 5.00% of any installment of interest not received by Lender within ten (10) business days of the applicable due date shall be assessed.

**Total Project Cost:** \$425,000,000

Lender shall have \"last money in\" priority such that all equity is expended on Project costs before any loan proceeds are advanced.

**[Section 4: Security / Collateral]{.underline}**

The Loan shall be secured by, and Lender shall have a perfected first-priority security interest in, the following collateral:

**First Priority Leasehold Mortgage.** A first-priority leasehold deed of trust or mortgage (the \"Leasehold Mortgage\") encumbering Borrower\'s entire leasehold interest in the Premises under the ground lease by and between the City of Port Calloway Redevelopment Authority, as Landlord, and Meridian Gateway Holdings LLC, as Tenant (the \"Ground Lease\"), including all improvements, fixtures, and appurtenances now or hereafter constructed on, affixed to, or located upon the Premises.

**Assignment of Leases and Rents.** A first-priority collateral assignment of all subleases, rental agreements, rents, revenues, issues, profits, and other income arising from the Project.

**Assignment of Construction Contracts and Plans.** A collateral assignment of the general construction contract, all major subcontracts, all architectural and engineering agreements, and all project plans, drawings, specifications, and permits relating to the construction and operation of the Project, together with consent to assignment from each applicable counterparty.

**Pledge of Borrower Interests.** A first-priority pledge of one hundred percent (100%) of the membership interests in Meridian Gateway Holdings LLC, together with the organizational documents and any applicable equity agreements.

**Environmental Indemnity Agreement.** An unsecured environmental indemnity agreement executed by Borrower and each Guarantor in favor of Lender, indemnifying Lender against all environmental liabilities, claims, costs, and expenses arising from or relating to the Project or the Premises.

**Completion Guaranty.** A completion guaranty executed by Coventry Capital Partners LP in favor of Lender, guaranteeing lien-free completion of the Project in accordance with the approved plans and budget on or before the Initial Maturity Date (as extended, if applicable).

**Carve-Out Guaranty.** A limited recourse guaranty executed by Marcus Ellison (individually) in favor of Lender, covering customary non-recourse carve-out obligations, including without limitation: fraud, intentional misrepresentation, misappropriation of funds, willful misconduct, environmental liability, voluntary bankruptcy filing by Borrower or any constituent member, prohibited transfers of the leasehold interest or ownership interests, and misapplication of insurance proceeds or condemnation awards.

**Letter of Credit / Security Deposit.** Evidence satisfactory to Lender that Borrower has posted (or will post prior to or simultaneously with closing) an irrevocable standby letter of credit in the amount of \$5,700,000 (or, at Borrower\'s option, a cash security deposit in such amount) with the Authority, as required under the Ground Lease.

**[Section 5: Required Ground Lease Provisions]{.underline}**

Lender requires that the Ground Lease between the City of Port Calloway Redevelopment Authority (as Landlord) and Meridian Gateway Holdings LLC (as Tenant), the term sheet for which is dated June 10, 2025, include each of the following provisions, every one of which shall constitute a condition precedent to the closing of the Loan. The Ground Lease, in its final executed form, shall be in form and substance satisfactory to Lender and Lender\'s counsel in all respects.

**5.1 Leasehold Mortgage Consent**

The Ground Lease shall expressly permit Tenant to grant a first-priority leasehold mortgage to Lender and its successors and assigns, without the prior consent, approval, or joinder of Landlord and without the payment of any consent fee, administrative charge, or other compensation to Landlord. No approval, consent, or other condition from Landlord shall be required for the recording, enforcement, or foreclosure of the Leasehold Mortgage. The Leasehold Mortgage shall be permitted to encumber the entire leasehold interest created by the Ground Lease, together with all improvements, fixtures, and appurtenances now or hereafter constructed on or located upon the Premises.

**5.2 Subordination, Non-Disturbance, and Attornment Agreement (SNDA)**

Landlord shall execute and deliver, simultaneously with or prior to the first advance of Loan proceeds, a Subordination, Non-Disturbance, and Attornment Agreement (the \"SNDA\") in form and substance acceptable to Lender and Lender\'s counsel, containing at a minimum the following provisions:

> \(a\) Landlord\'s written acknowledgment of the existence and priority of the Leasehold Mortgage and recognition of Lender\'s interest therein;
>
> \(b\) Landlord\'s agreement not to disturb Lender\'s security interest or the rights of any purchaser at a foreclosure sale or transferee pursuant to a deed in lieu of foreclosure, so long as the obligations of Tenant under the Ground Lease continue to be performed;
>
> \(c\) Landlord\'s agreement to recognize Lender, or its designee, or any purchaser at foreclosure or transferee pursuant to a deed in lieu of foreclosure, as Tenant under the Ground Lease upon the same terms and conditions as the Ground Lease; and
>
> \(d\) Such additional provisions as Lender may reasonably require, including provisions relating to casualty, condemnation, and insurance proceeds.

**5.3 New Lease Right**

The Ground Lease shall provide that if the Ground Lease is terminated for any reason whatsoever, including without limitation Tenant default, surrender, rejection in bankruptcy, operation of law, or otherwise, Lender (or its designee) shall have the right, upon written request delivered to Landlord within sixty (60) days after Lender\'s receipt of notice of such termination, to enter into a new ground lease (the \"New Lease\") with Landlord on the same terms and conditions as the terminated Ground Lease for the remainder of the original term (including any extension periods), provided that:

> \(a\) Lender (or its designee) cures all monetary defaults then existing under the Ground Lease within sixty (60) days after the effective date of the New Lease;
>
> \(b\) Lender (or its designee) cures all non-monetary defaults that are reasonably susceptible of cure within ninety (90) days after the effective date of the New Lease, or, if such cure cannot reasonably be completed within such ninety (90)-day period, Lender (or its designee) commences such cure within such ninety (90)-day period and thereafter diligently and continuously pursues cure to completion within a reasonable time, but in no event more than one hundred eighty (180) days after the effective date of the New Lease;
>
> \(c\) Lender (or its designee) assumes all obligations under the New Lease prospectively from the effective date of the New Lease; and
>
> \(d\) The New Lease shall have a priority in all respects equal to the priority of the terminated Ground Lease, and all subleases, licenses, and occupancy agreements entered into by Tenant or any subtenant prior to the termination of the Ground Lease shall be recognized by Landlord under the New Lease.

Landlord shall be required to execute and deliver the New Lease within thirty (30) days following Lender\'s written request therefor, and the New Lease shall be effective as of the date of termination of the Ground Lease.

**5.4 Lender Cure Rights / Notice Requirements**

The Ground Lease shall require that Landlord provide Lender with copies of all notices of default, notices of termination, and any other material notices delivered to Tenant under the Ground Lease simultaneously with delivery of such notices to Tenant, sent to Lender at: Bayside Federal Lending Corp., 200 Atlantic Boulevard, Stamford, CT 06902, Attention: Sandra Milliken, Senior Vice President, Commercial Real Estate Lending, with a copy to Lender\'s counsel at such address as Lender may from time to time designate.

No termination of the Ground Lease shall be effective unless and until Lender has received such notice and the applicable Lender cure periods described below have expired without cure by Lender:

> \(a\) **Monetary Defaults.** Lender shall have sixty (60) days from Lender\'s receipt of notice of any monetary default under the Ground Lease to cure such monetary default on behalf of Tenant.
>
> \(b\) **Non-Monetary Defaults.** Lender shall have ninety (90) days from Lender\'s receipt of notice of any non-monetary default under the Ground Lease to cure such non-monetary default on behalf of Tenant, or, if such cure cannot reasonably be completed within such ninety (90)-day period, Lender shall have commenced cure within such ninety (90)-day period and shall thereafter diligently and continuously pursue cure to completion within a reasonable time.

The foregoing Lender cure periods shall run in addition to, and not concurrent with, any cure periods afforded to Tenant under the Ground Lease. Landlord shall accept cure by Lender as if such cure had been performed by Tenant.

**5.5 Prohibition on Voluntary Surrender and Amendment**

The Ground Lease shall provide that, for so long as the Leasehold Mortgage remains in effect, Landlord shall not accept a voluntary surrender of the Ground Lease by Tenant, and Landlord and Tenant shall not amend, modify, supplement, or terminate the Ground Lease in any material respect, without the prior written consent of Lender. Any purported surrender, amendment, modification, supplement, or termination of the Ground Lease effected without the prior written consent of Lender shall be void and of no force or effect as against Lender, and the Ground Lease shall continue in full force and effect as if such purported surrender, amendment, modification, supplement, or termination had not occurred.

**5.6 Right to Foreclose and Assign**

Lender shall have the unconditional right to foreclose (whether by judicial foreclosure, power of sale, or otherwise) or accept a deed in lieu of foreclosure of the Leasehold Mortgage, and to assign the Ground Lease to a qualified transferee at or following any foreclosure sale or deed-in-lieu transfer, without the prior consent of Landlord, provided that such transferee meets reasonable financial and experience qualifications substantially similar to those required of Borrower at the time the Ground Lease was executed. Landlord shall not unreasonably withhold, condition, or delay recognition of any such transferee as Tenant under the Ground Lease. The Ground Lease shall expressly provide that no foreclosure, deed-in-lieu transfer, or assignment by Lender or Lender\'s designee shall require Landlord approval, and that Landlord shall execute any documents reasonably requested by Lender to effectuate or confirm such foreclosure, transfer, or assignment.

**5.7 Bankruptcy Protections**

The Ground Lease shall include provisions ensuring that, if Tenant becomes a debtor in any proceeding under the United States Bankruptcy Code (Title 11, U.S.C.) or any similar state insolvency law:

> \(a\) Lender shall have the right to request that any trustee, debtor-in-possession, or other party-in-interest assume or reject the Ground Lease in a timely manner consistent with the requirements of 11 U.S.C. § 365;
>
> \(b\) Lender shall have the right to cure any defaults under the Ground Lease and to provide adequate assurance of future performance on behalf of Tenant to the extent necessary to prevent rejection of the Ground Lease; and
>
> \(c\) The New Lease provisions set forth in Section 5.3 above shall survive rejection of the Ground Lease in bankruptcy to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, and Landlord shall recognize Lender\'s right to obtain a New Lease notwithstanding such rejection.

The following conditions must be satisfied to the satisfaction of Lender and its counsel prior to the initial advance of Loan proceeds:

(or another nationally recognized title insurance company acceptable to Lender) in the amount of the Loan (\$285,000,000), insuring the first-priority lien of the Leasehold Mortgage upon Borrower\'s leasehold interest in the Premises, with endorsements customarily required by institutional construction lenders, and subject to no exceptions other than those specifically reviewed and approved by Lender in writing. Acknowledgment of the Environmental Land Use Restriction (\"ELUR\") recorded at Volume 412, Page 88, Port Calloway Land Records, together with written confirmation from Lender\'s environmental consultant that the proposed development is consistent with the terms and restrictions of the ELUR.

> \(g\) Delivery of an approved construction budget and schedule, together with a fully-executed guaranteed maximum price general construction contract (or other construction contract structure acceptable to Lender), and evidence of all required governmental permits, approvals, and authorizations necessary for commencement of construction of the Project.

> \(h\) Evidence of required insurance coverages, including without limitation: Builder\'s Risk insurance in an amount not less than the total hard construction costs; Commercial General Liability insurance with combined single limits of not less than \$10,000,000 per occurrence and \$20,000,000 in the aggregate; Environmental Liability insurance with limits of not less than \$5,000,000 per occurrence and \$10,000,000 in the aggregate; Flood Insurance for FEMA Flood Zone AE as required by the National Flood Insurance Program and in amounts satisfactory to Lender; and Workers\' Compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Lender shall be named as an additional insured and/or loss payee, as applicable, on all such policies.
